newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia police storm drug lord's "White House".
newsitem.headline: Colombia police storm drug lord's "White House".

text.p: Colombian security services on Thursday stormed a sprawling mansion modelled after Washington's White House that belonged to one of the late leaders of the Cali drug mob, officials said.

Jose "Chepe" Santacruz, the former No.3 of the powerful Cali cartel, brought in foreign architects to build the house and paid for its sumptuous styling with his cut of the proceeds from the drug mafia's worldwide cocaine sales.

Work on the replica "White House," in one of Cali's most luxurious residential districts, was cut short, however, when Santacruz was gunned down by police in March 1996, two months after he slipped out of Bogota's top-security La Picota jail.

An elite force from the state security service DAS occupied the building, which covers an entire city block, as part of an operation to confiscate more than 300 of the late drug lord's properties, said to be worth more than $20 million.
"The building was only half-finished but it has a facade very similar to the U.S. White House. It's full of statues and sculptures," a regional DAS official told reporters.
The interior of the mansion was covered with Italian tiles and imported marble slabs. A fully equipped gym and top-of-the-line kitchen items had been delivered but never unpacked, the official said.

Santacruz helped his bosses, the notorious Rodriguez Orejuela brothers, transform the Cali cartel into one of the world's most lucrative criminal empires responsible for an estimated 80 percent of the global cocaine supply, according to U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration figures.

He was captured by police in June 1995, but climbed through a prison window and strolled to freedom in January 1996, in one of Colombia's most infamous jailbreaks. He was shot to death two months later at a police roadblock near the northwest city of Medellin.
